intro: Professionals and everyday users convert foot-pounds (ft·lbf) to joules (J) when working across imperial and si standards in residential electricity billing, HVAC heating load calculations, battery storage sizing, and nutritional energy tracking. One foot-pound (ft·lbf) equals 1.355818 joules, while 1 joule equals 0.737562 foot-pounds. Whether you are verifying energy specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor vs. Early Rounding Drift
items: The exact conversion factor from Foot-pound (ft·lbf) to Joule is 1.35581795, derived from the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement (1 inch = 25.4 mm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).

In structural engineering, CNC machining, or bulk inventory totals, rounding the multiplier to 2 decimal places too early can introduce cumulative tolerance errors; always compute with the full factor and round only the final displayed figure.

faqs.question: How many joules (J) are in 1 foot-pound (ft·lbf) (ft·lbf)?
faqs.answer: There are 1.35581795 joules (J) in 1 foot-pound (ft·lbf) (ft·lbf), which rounds to 1.3558 J for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 joule equals 0.737562 foot-pounds.

faqs.question: How do I convert foot-pounds to joules (ft·lbf to J)?
faqs.answer: To convert foot-pounds to joules, use the formula: J = ft·lbf × 1.35581795. For example, converting 500 ft·lbf gives 677.909 J.

faqs.question: What is 500 foot-pounds in joules?
faqs.answer: 500 foot-pounds (ft·lbf) equals exactly 677.909 joules (J) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
